sections.overview: Phalacrocorax varius is Australia's Australian Pied Cormorant.
sections.identification: It has a black back, white belly and grey hooked bill.
sections.habitat: It uses coasts, estuaries, mangroves and eastern inland wetlands.
sections.diet: It eats mostly fish, also crustaceans and molluscs.
sections.behavior: It dives with webbed feet and spreads its wings to dry.
sections.reproduction: It nests colonially; both parents incubate eggs and feed young.
sections.ecology: P. fuscescens is restricted to southern coasts. P. varius also uses eastern inland wetlands.
sections.conservation: BirdLife Australia reports its global IUCN category as Least Concern.
